items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: we had an accident and Cecil Irwin was killed -- one of the tenor players in Earl's band.

ctx.x: But we had -- I know we had a little half a pint of liquor, and we went out to 63rd and Stony. Ray went out with me late at night to catch this late train at night -- riding into New York. But Ray walked out -- came out to the station with me.

So, he encouraged me to go. Yeah, Ray and I were -- and Budd Johnson was on that band to. How Budd got in the band was we had an accident and Cecil Irwin was killed -- one of the tenor players in Earl's band. He was killed out right, you know. A grain truck side-swiped us in Iowa. We were going from -- we were playing theaters. We were on a theater tour there. And this was '33, the latter part of '33.

We were going from DesMoines. We just closed a theater in DesMoines. We were going to Minneapolis to open another theater. And we were playing -- but the show -- it was a show. And the Mills Brothers were on the show. And at that -- on that same show was a -- was the Palmer Brothers were singing too with Earl's band. I don't know if you ever heard of them -- singers. Well, they sang with Cab Calloway later. One crippled little boy was with them -- Clarence. And they really sang good, you know. And also Tip, Tap,…
